s01: Agent API, end to end. One HTTP API now runs the web page, the terminal chat, and your own programs. Let us see it work, open first, then locked down.
s02: Open mode is the default on your own machine. If you bind it to every network interface, the server warns you loudly at startup. Anyone who can reach it could chat with the agent. Here, whoami says everyone is the one local user, and invoke gives an answer with no token at all.
s03: Token mode. With no token the server answers four oh one. With the shared secret you are the admin. And with manage tokens switched on, an admin can mint a named token over the API, with a lifetime. That token is a chat token, so asking it to manage tokens is refused with four oh three.
s04: Two guards sit in front of every route, and they are cbSecurity's own middleware. Here the rate limit is three calls a minute. The fourth call is answered four twenty nine, with a Retry After header. The address allow list works the same way and answers four oh three.
s05: From BoxLang, there is a documented client with one method for every route. This script checks health, calls the agent, streams a reply, lists conversations, and creates and revokes a token.
s06: The API describes itself. The server hands out an Open API three document, made from the same list that writes the routes, so the two cannot drift apart.
s07: Now the web page, on the same API. In token mode it asks for the password in a form, not a browser prompt. The header is quiet, with one settings gear. Suggestions send with one click. Settings holds the conversation actions, your notes and appearance, and for an admin, the access tokens panel, where a new secret is shown once.
s08: The terminal chat talks to the same API. Conversations, notes, the context ring and every slash command are shared with the page, so you can start a chat in one place and pick it up in the other. Here is a short session: the keys, the context, naming and forking a conversation.
s09: And chat platforms use it too. A gateway keeps each person's memory apart, makes every platform thread its own conversation, and lists the chat on the shared conversation list, marked with the platform. These are the gateway session tests, running.
s10: That is the whole path: open or token, guarded by cbSecurity, described by Open API, called from curl, BoxLang, the page, the terminal and chat platforms. One API.
